hypothesis.title: currency 2.0.3 rollout missing currency_conversion.json causes crash loop
hypothesis.summary: Currency service version 2.0.3 was deployed 8 minutes before the alert and immediately began crash-looping because the release is missing the required currency_conversion.json data file. The pod exits with "std::runtime_error: missing currency_conversion.json" and enters CrashLoopBackOff. Because currency is called by frontend (and checkout) for price conversions on nearly every page, frontend's error rate spiked from 0.4% to 63.5%. This is a repeat of postmortem PM-2026-08-02 where currency 2.0.1 had the same packaging error.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend's 5xx error rate, but frontend is a victim. Traces show 99% of failing frontend requests end in currency errors. The currency service deployed version 2.0.3 eight minutes before the alert, and immediately after that deployment currency pods entered CrashLoopBackOff with 6 restarts. The error message is explicit: "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error': missing currency_conversion.json". This matches postmortem PM-2026-08-02 exactly—a previous currency release (2.0.1) also shipped without the required data file and caused the same crash loop and frontend error spike. Currency's request rate dropped from 38 req/s to 1.6 req/s because the pod is crashing and unavailable most of the time. The checkout service also restarted once (exit 137, likely OOMKilled), but that is unrelated—checkout's own error rate is not shown, and the frontend errors are explicitly traced to currency calls. The flagd stream errors in frontend logs are a red herring (started 44 minutes before the alert, unrelated to the currency deploy). This is a bad deploy that introduced a crash loop due to a missing configuration file.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Currency deployed version 2.0.3 exactly 8 minutes before the alert, timing matches the start of errors.
Currency pod is in CrashLoopBackOff with 6 restarts and exit code 1, confirming the container cannot start successfully.
Currency logs show FATAL errors with the exact message 'missing currency_conversion.json', identifying the root cause of the crash.
Failing trace shows frontend calling currency and receiving the same 'missing currency_conversion.json' error, proving the error propagates upstream.
99% (132 of 133) of failing frontend traces terminate in currency, confirming currency is the origin of the errors, not just a symptom.
Currency request rate dropped 95% (38 req/s to 1.6 req/s) because the crashing pod is unavailable, consistent with CrashLoopBackOff behavior.

suggested_actions.title: Rollback currency deployment to previous version 2.0.2
suggested_actions.rationale: Version 2.0.2 was stable before the deploy. This is the safest and fastest mitigation, matching the resolution in PM-2026-08-02 for the identical issue.

suggested_actions.title: Verify currency pods are healthy after rollback
suggested_actions.rationale: Confirm that the rolled-back pods start successfully and exit CrashLoopBackOff, and that frontend error rate returns to baseline.

suggested_actions.title: Investigate currency 2.0.3 build artifacts for missing data file
suggested_actions.rationale: Check the CI/CD pipeline and container image for version 2.0.3 to confirm currency_conversion.json was not packaged. Fix the build process before attempting to redeploy 2.0.3.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Checkout did restart once (exit 137, likely OOMKilled), but there is no evidence of checkout being the error origin. Frontend traces show 99% of errors terminate in currency, not checkout. The checkout restart is likely a side effect or unrelated issue.
